title: React Complete Cheat Sheet
description: Comprehensive quick reference covering React components, hooks, state management, patterns, performance optimization, and testing.

data.text: React components are the building blocks of any React application. They accept inputs (props) and return React elements describing what should appear on screen.

data.title: Functional component
Class component

Component composition

data.text: The useState hook lets you add state to functional components. It returns a state variable and a function to update it.

data.text: useEffect lets you perform side effects in functional components. It replaces componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, and componentWillUnmount.

data.text: useRef returns a mutable ref object that persists for the component's lifetime. It can access DOM elements directly or store mutable values.

data.title: useRef for DOM access

data.text: useContext lets you subscribe to React context without introducing nesting. Context provides a way to pass data through the component tree without prop drilling.

data.title: Create and provide context

data.text: useReducer is an alternative to useState for complex state logic. It accepts a reducer function and returns the current state paired with a dispatch method.

data.title: useReducer basic

data.text: useMemo memoizes expensive calculations. It only recalculates the value when one of the dependencies changes.

data.title: useMemo for expensive computation

data.text: useCallback memoizes event handler functions. It returns a memoized version of the callback that only changes if dependencies change.

data.text: Custom hooks let you extract component logic into reusable functions. They must start with 'use' and can call other hooks.

data.text: React.memo is a higher-order component that memoizes the rendered output. It prevents re-renders when props haven't changed.

data.text: Concurrent React features that let you prioritize updates. useTransition marks state updates as non-urgent. useDeferredValue defers a value.

data.text: Rendering lists in React requires a unique key prop for each item to help React identify which items have changed.
